Ben continued: "There are things that we do there and there, but there are so many advantages. Whoever is behind these courses that we put them through, they are safe as houses compared to what runners get coming up against at our dojo."
Introducing challenging and risky activities into an engaging live setting increases the likelihood of competitors taking unwarranted risks; however, starting new participants in a safe, properly supervised and fulfilling environment is crucial to meeting the show's development objectives.
And Ben stated that labeling ITV's Ninja Warrior as fail fast and tough love would be incongruous.
"It's not 'if' you fail. So many things have safety measures in place, and it filters out too many people and is not the safest environment, whereas here we build these things on the back of the versions and you have to be very fit and very, very agile and three or four people in one team usually - and we deliver what those contestants and the audience want."
Rochelle, who dazzled with aerial acrobatics during her audition run, stated that performing the final segment on the Banzai Wall was the showcase's most formidable challenge for her.
"Junior, the stunt guy who came and talked us through the course, said that in a real live obstacle course I'd have lost a shoe running it, and I maybe would have slipped and fallen. Here the stakes are possible failure, no failure, but here you have a whole bunch of guidance so you're thinking there are lots of things wrong with that."
